newsitem.title: FRANCE: BoF's Trichet says French interest rates low.
newsitem.headline: BoF's Trichet says French interest rates low.

text.p: Bank of France Governor Jean-Claude Trichet said on Tuesday that French interest rates were very low and the central Bank would do whatever was needed to keep financial market rates low.
In an interview with Reuters Financial Television, he also said that it was important that a single European currency be a solid and credible as Europe's most credible currencies.
"We have a very low level, obviously, of interest rates and we will do whatever is needed to preserve our low level of market rates," Trichet said.
"I don't think the credibility of the euro has been damaged and I am of the opinion we are on track," he said.
"We are directly interested in having a solid euro, a euro which inspires confidence," he said.
"I am totally confident that the euro has to be as solid, credible and confidence-inspiring as is the franc today or naturally the deutschemark today or the guilder today," Trichet said.

"Because to create the best basis for solid growth, for stable, strong growth, you need low market interest rates and you will not get low market interest rates if you have a euro which is not solid and credible," he said.
